newsitem.title: FRANCE: French union leader wants layoff funds frozen.
newsitem.headline: French union leader wants layoff funds frozen.

text.p: Marc Blondel, leader of France's powerful Force Ouvriere trade union, urged the government on Thursday to suspend special subsidies for laid-off workers until September, when the government is due to announce its jobs programme.
He said that suspending the processing of companies' demands for so-called FNE subsidies (Fonds national pour l'emploi) would prevent the companies from carrying out planned layoffs.

"If the prefects block the FNEs, you are going to see the job layoff plans blocked," he told France Inter radio. Prefects are national government representatives who administer at the departmental level.
Socialist Prime Minister Lionel Jospin has delayed until autumn key decisions on how his new leftist government will carry out a campaign promise to create 700,000 new jobs.
He said he needed the extra time to assess the condition of public finances.

Blondel charged that Jospin's decision was prompting some companies to begin carrying out "preventive layoffs" -- acting quickly in order to beat any possible future restrictions on their ability to slim down payrolls.
He said the availability of the FNE funds was an additional incentive to lay off workers.

"They are proposing layoffs in anticipation (of Jospin's programme) and they are going to come looking for money," he said. "The prefect can simply say, 'I refuse your job lay-off plans. I refuse to pay the FNE starting right now'."

French Communist Party leader Robert Hue this week asked Jospin to order prefects to stop processing job layoff plans, which companies are required by law to prepare when they intend to lay off workers.
But Jospin said such a move would be illegal.
Blondel said he disagreed with Jospin's conclusion but set out his proposal as an alternative.
